title: SQL: SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY
welcome_lead: Speak fluently to a relational database.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY and HAVING.
final_note: These five keywords cover most everyday queries.

concepts.def: SQL clause choosing which columns to return.
SQL clause filtering rows before grouping.
SQL clause combining rows from two tables on a condition.
SQL clause grouping rows for aggregate functions.
SQL clause filtering groups after aggregation.
Function like COUNT, SUM or AVG operating on groups.

walkthroughs.body_html: SELECT name, age FROM students WHERE age >= 18; returns columns name and age for adult students. WHERE filters rows before any grouping happens.
INNER JOIN returns rows matching in both tables. LEFT JOIN keeps every row of the left table, padding unmatched right-side columns with NULL.
GROUP BY course partitions rows by course. Aggregates like COUNT(*) apply per group. HAVING filters the resulting groups — unlike WHERE, which filters individual rows.
